formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h2 : distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) (h3 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) : (∠ a:b:c + ∠ a:b:d : ℝ) = ∟ + ∟ := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ (d ≠ b)) → ((∠ c:b:a + ∠ a:b:d : ℝ) = ∟ + ∟)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) (h2 : a ≠ b) (h3 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) (h4 : c ≠ b) (h5 : d ≠ b) : (∠ c:b:a + ∠ a:b:d : ℝ) = ∟ + ∟ := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), (((a ≠ b)) ∧ (a.onLine AB) ∧ (b.onLine AB) ∧ (c.onLine CD) ∧ (d.onLine CD) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) ∧ (between c b d)) → ((∠ a:b:c : ℝ) + (∠ a:b:d : ℝ) = ∟ + ∟)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : (a ≠ b)) (h2 : a.onLine AB) (h3 : b.onLine AB) (h4 : c.onLine CD) (h5 : d.onLine CD) (h6 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) (h7 : between c b d) : (∠ a:b:c : ℝ) + (∠ a:b:d : ℝ) = ∟ + ∟ := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (¬(AB).intersectsLine (CD))) → (((∠ a:c:b : ℝ) + (∠ a:c:d : ℝ) = ∟ + ∟))

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine b c CD) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (d ≠ b) ∧ (¬ (∠ a:b:c = ∟ ∧ ∠ a:b:d = ∟))) → ((∠ a:b:c + ∠ a:b:d) = ∟ + ∟)

reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line), AB ≠ CD ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a b AB ∧ distinctPointsOnLine c d CD ∧ between d b c → ∠ c:b:a + ∠ a:b:d = ∟ + ∟
nl_statement: If a straight-line stood on a(nother)  straight-line makes angles, it will certainly either make two right-angles, or (angles whose sum is) equal to two right-angles. For  let some straight-line $AB$ stood on the straight-line $CD$ make the angles $CBA$ and $ABD$. I say that the angles $CBA$ and $ABD$ are certainly either two right-angles, or (have a sum) equal to two right-angles. <prf> Thus, (the sum of) $ABD$ and $ABC$ is also equal to two right-angles.Thus, if a straight-line stood on a(nother)  straight-line makes angles, it will certainly either make two right-angles, or (angles whose sum is) equal to two right-angles.
